claims.summary: British Council states that participle clauses use present, past or perfect participles; their tense is indicated by the main verb; when no other subject appears, the participle and main-clause verb have the same subject.
British Council documents present participle clauses for result, reason, simultaneous action and additional information about the main-clause subject, with the cited examples.
British Council states that past participles normally have passive meaning and perfect participle clauses show an action completed before the main-clause action.
